source.what: Joby Aviation news article page (Blade BLADEone / Aero partnership announcement) — distilled for its GRID and TYPE system only. The entry encodes the corrected system the page points at, not the page's faults.
source.method: Chromium (ms-playwright chromium-1234) driven by puppeteer-core, one isolated browser context per width, no shared state. Six viewports captured: 1440, 1200, 1024, 834, 600, 390 (deviceScaleFactor 1 for measurement, 2-3 for stills). Per viewport: full-page and above-the-fold JPEG stills, computed styles via getComputedStyle for every grid container and its direct children, getBoundingClientRect for box geometry, grid-template-columns / column-gap / padding read directly off the resolved computed style, per-child grid-column and grid-area read back to derive column spans. Page scrolled end to end before measurement (all entrance animations finished, not frozen) so no element was measured in a pre-animation state. 16-column placements derived by matching each child's x offset against the computed track starts, not by reading markup.
gaps: No design-token source, Figma file, or CSS custom-property dump exists for this site; every value here is read off rendered computed styles, so authored intent cannot be distinguished from accident.

The full-page desktop capture does not contain the footer's text. The footer text was still measured live via computed styles and DOM (see evidence below); the missing text is an artifact of the capture path (a full-bleed colour band below the footer's creative section), not of the page.

Column spans at 1024w and below were derived from a grid whose tracks resolve to 0px with a 100px column-gap, so track-index arithmetic is unreliable below 1024; those placements are reported from grid-column values instead.
Hover, focus, and open-menu states were not captured for layout purposes.
Only one page of the site was captured. The 16-column grid, gutter, and type scale were confirmed on this page only; whether other templates share them is unverified.
source.notes: SCOPE. This entry grades horizontal grid, vertical rhythm, and typography. Color, imagery, motion, and copy carry no scales and no values: their canon scales are null with reasons rather than guessed. The page's own faults are treated as negative evidence that justifies a rule, never as the target — see the rules in layout, structure, and type. Where the page and its own system disagree, the system wins in every target.

parts.name: The 16-track field
parts.description: Every horizontal band on the page — nav, hero, media, standfirst, article, sidebar, card section, footer — resolves to the same 16-column grid with the same fixed px tracks and the same constant column gap. There is no per-section grid. The page's whole horizontal identity is that one field, and every block's left and right edge is a track edge.
parts.entry_test: Delete the 16-track field and every band degrades to ad-hoc widths — the page stops looking like itself. The field is the single gesture the page repeats in every section.
parts.recipe: Declare the grid once on a shared page container and let every band inherit it: display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(16, 70px); column-gap: 16px; padding-inline: 40px. At 1200w the track becomes 55px, at 1024w 44px; gap and gutter stay 16px and 40px. Verified exact: 1440 - 80 = 1360 = 16*70 + 15*16; 1200 - 80 = 1120 = 16*55 + 15*16; 1024 - 80 = 944 = 16*44 + 15*16. Never redeclare the grid inside a section: a section that redeclares it is how this page acquired two incompatible placement systems on one set of tracks.

checks.check: Every full-width band (nav, hero, media caption, standfirst, article, sidebar, card section, footer) resolves to the same 16-track grid
Tracks are fixed px (70/55/44 at 1440/1200/1024), not fr or %
Column gap is 16px at every width at or above 834
Page gutter is 40px at 1440, 1200 and 1024
Content band width equals 16 tracks plus 15 gaps exactly (1360 at 1440)

evidence: 1440w computed grid-template-columns: 70px x16 on heroContent, newsArticleBody, newsArticleContentSection, sectionNews and footer alike
identical column-gap 16px reported on all five grid containers

parts.name: Placement by column span, not by content width
parts.description: Every block is placed by declaring a column span on the shared field. The page uses a small, reused span vocabulary — 2 (rail, 156px), 7 (section heading, 586px), 8 (article measure, 672px and caption, 672px), 12 (hero headline, 1016px), 16 (full content band, 1360px) — and blocks align to track edges, not to each other's widths.
parts.entry_test: Remove span placement and blocks size themselves from content; the page's edges stop landing on each other. The span vocabulary is what makes the layout readable as one system.
parts.recipe: Set grid-column on the child, e.g. grid-column: 1 / span 12 for a hero headline, 5 / span 8 for the article measure, 1 / span 2 for the rail, 1 / span 16 for a full band. Derive left edges from the span, never from a pixel width. Where text must not exceed a comfortable measure, cap it with max-width inside its span rather than resizing the span. Never place a major block with a flex content width — measured on this page, the card row's three items resolve to 559 / 458 / 343px, a 1.63:1 spread, none of which lands on a track start (the second begins at x=599, where no column begins).

checks.check: Every direct child of a grid band declares grid-column, or is an intentional full-bleed escape
No major block's left edge falls between track starts
Span vocabulary is small and reused (2, 7, 8, 12, 16 observed) rather than one span per block
Sibling blocks in one band share a track edge where the design intends alignment (rail at column 1, measure at column 5)
Card-row items are equal spans or a declared span pattern, not content-derived widths

parts.name: The article column is exactly span 8
parts.description: Body text occupies columns 5 through 12, which is 672px at 1440w, with the side rail on columns 1-2 and columns 3-4 held empty as the gutter between rail and text. The blank columns are structural, not accidental: they are what separates the rail from the measure.
parts.entry_test: Let the text run wider and the rail crowds it; let it run narrower and the empty columns read as a mistake. The exact 8-column measure is what makes the article band legible as designed rather than fitted.
parts.recipe: grid-column: 5 / span 8 on the text column; rail at 1 / span 2; leave 3-4 empty. Article measure is then 8*70 + 7*16 = 672px at 1440w. Text inside the span may carry a max-width cap (the page declares max-width: 760px on the span-8 parent, which never binds because the span is narrower than the cap) but the span itself must not change. If a block inside the article needs to be wider than the measure, widen it on a shared rule that overhangs symmetrically, not on one block.

parts.name: One fluid multiplier, held across the whole scale
parts.description: Below its fixed-track tier the page does not step its values; it multiplies them all by one factor. At 834w every measured value — track width 35.83px, column gap 13.03px, gutter 32.58px, h1 65.16px, body 13.03px — is the 1024w value times 0.8145. At 390w every value is the 600w value times 0.65. Type, gutter, gap and tracks travel together.
parts.entry_test: Step only the type and leave the grid, and the measure drifts against the columns; step only the grid and the type breaks its ratio. The single multiplier is what keeps the system proportional while it shrinks.

anchor.value: html / :root (the single scale that every band inherits)

parts.recipe: Drive the whole system from one scale factor per breakpoint tier. Fixed tiers: 1440 track 70px, 1200 track 55px, 1024 track 44px, gutter 40px throughout, gap 16px throughout. Below the fixed tier, multiply every value by the tier factor (0.8145 in this design's middle tier, 0.65 in its small tier) rather than restating each value. Express values as calc() off one custom property so the factor cannot drift between grid and type. Return gap and gutter to their unscaled constants (16px and 40px) at the mobile tier, where the page reverts to 6 tracks and a fixed 16px gutter.

checks.check: At the middle tier, track, gap, gutter, h1 and body are all the previous-tier value times one common factor
The factor is expressed once (a single custom property or calc base), not restated per value
At the mobile tier, gutter returns to 16px and column gap to 8.32px rather than continuing the multiplier
Display-to-body size ratio is unchanged across the fluid tiers
Grid and type shrink by the same factor (no drift between measure and columns)

evidence: mobile tier overrides: 390w gutter 16.64px (= 16 x 1.04 vw-relative split, not the 0.65 factor), column gap 8.32px

parts.name: Fixed rails at the outer columns
parts.description: The system reserves its outermost columns for optional furniture: column 1-2 for a left rail, columns 15-16 for a right cluster, so a band can carry a rail or sit empty without the main block moving. The footer uses all four of those rails at once — 1, 11, 13, 15 — and the article uses 1-2 with 15-16 empty.
parts.entry_test: Remove the reserved outer rails and furniture starts pushing the main column; the layout's stability under varying content comes from those columns being held.
parts.recipe: Reserve span 2 at column 1 and span 2 ending at column 16 as optional furniture slots. Main content starts at column 5 when a left rail is present and column 1 when it is not; the right cluster ends flush at column 16. Critical: a band with furniture on rails must not leave an unaccounted void between the rail clusters. The footer here places its four lists on rails 1 / 11 / 13 / 15 and leaves columns 3 through 10 (x 250 to 860, about 700px) empty on row 1, which is a rail system used without a rule for the space between. When a band carries furniture on both sides, the interior space must be a declared span (a spacer, a divider, or nothing at all — not a hole).

checks.check: Rails occupy span 2 at column 1 and span 2 ending at column 16
Main content's left edge is a track start whether or not a rail is present
A band with furniture on both sides accounts for the interior columns as a declared span
No band leaves an interior void wider than one track unaccounted for
A rail carrying no content collapses the main block left rather than leaving the rail reserved and empty

parts.name: Grid rows baseline their items
parts.description: When a band puts two blocks on one grid row, their tops align to the track row, not to their own content heights. Rows are declared, so the vertical space between rows is a set value rather than the leftover of a fixed band height.
parts.entry_test: Let row items float to their own heights and a band reads as two unrelated halves; the row is what makes a two-sided band read as one line of content.
parts.recipe: Declare grid-template-rows or rely on align-items: start with items that have no self-alignment margin. Both blocks on a row share a top edge; if one is a form and the other a logo, the form's first text baseline is offset from its own box top by a known amount so the pair still reads level. Never let a row's items resolve to different top offsets: this footer's row 2 puts the logo top at y 4566.1 and the newsletter top at y 4547.9 — an 18.2px offset between the two halves of one row. Keep row gaps explicit (this footer's two rows sit 525.8px apart because the row is implicit inside a fixed 900px band and absorbs all remaining height as one void).

parts.name: Two families, one size ratio
parts.description: One display family and one text family, and the display-to-body ratio is the same at every breakpoint: 5.0 at 1440 (80:16), 5.0 at 834 (65.16:13.03). The size ladder is a small set of steps off the body size, and the ratio between display and body is the whole of the type hierarchy.
parts.entry_test: Change the ratio at one breakpoint and the page stops reading as the same design at tablet width. The held ratio is the identity.
parts.recipe: Display family for headings only, text family for body and UI. Body 16px/1.4 (lh 22.4px); article title 80px/1.0; section heading 64px/1.0. Weight steps from a closed set of five: 400, 450, 500, 550 — no bold, nothing under 400. Hold display:body at the same ratio through every breakpoint (5.0 through the fixed and middle tiers). At the mobile tier the page's own ratio collapses to 2.125 because body jumps to 25.6px while h2 steps to only 51.2px — treat that as a fault, not a target; keep the ratio the same at every width. Cap display sizes at their fixed-tier value rather than letting them keep growing with the viewport.

parts.name: Tracking is a ratio of size
parts.description: Letter-spacing is derived from font size, not chosen per element: -3% at display sizes and -2% at text sizes. The 24px and 14px steps break to -1%, which is the tell that the rule was hand-applied rather than computed.
parts.entry_test: Drop the tracking and set sizes render loose at 80px and cramped at 12px; the derived rule is what keeps every size optically consistent.
parts.recipe: Compute letter-spacing from font-size rather than declaring it per selector: display sizes take -0.03em, text sizes -0.02em. At 80px that is -2.4px; 64px -1.92px; 18px -0.36px; 16px -0.32px; 12px -0.24px. The page declares 24px at -0.24px (-1%) and 14px at -0.14px (-1%) — two steps off the rule; normalise them to -0.02em so every size obeys the same derivation.

limitations: Scope is deliberately narrow: horizontal grid, vertical rhythm and typography. Colour, imagery, motion and copy are not graded — their canon scales carry null with a reason rather than a guessed value. The entry is built to be applied to an unrelated artifact to bring its structure and type into alignment, not to reproduce this page.

The entry encodes the corrected system, not the page as rendered. The page's card row places three items by flex content width (559 / 458 / 343px) and its footer leaves columns 3-10 empty on row 1 while reserving rails at both edges; both are recorded as the evidence behind never-rules, and neither is a target value.

The page uses three different column models (16 fixed px tracks, a 100px-gap fluid grid at 1024 and below, and 6 tracks at 600 and below). Only the 16-track model is encoded. The mobile 6-track model is described in evidence but not scored, because the page's own mobile tier collapses the display-to-body ratio to 2.125 and is treated as a fault.

No design-token source, Figma file or CSS custom-property dump was available. Every value is read from rendered computed styles, so authored intent cannot be separated from accident anywhere in this entry.

The vertical spacing ladder (8/16/24/32/48/64/96/128/160/200) is this entry's construction. The page has no spacing scale: its measured vertical values are 0.1, 21.8, 57, 89, 120, 140, 200 and 525.8px. The ladder is a rule imposed by the rubric, not a measurement of the source.

The span vocabulary (2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12, 16) and the track values are measured, but the page also uses spans outside it below 1024 (1/span 14, 1/span 6, 7/-1, 3/span 8) where its grid resolves to 0px tracks with a 100px gap; those placements are reported but not folded into the vocabulary.

The full-page desktop capture does not show the footer's text; the footer was measured live from the DOM and computed styles instead. The missing text is an artifact of the capture path, not of the page. No step of reading this entry requires the capture.
Only one page of the site was captured. The 16-track grid, 16px gap, 40px gutter and the type ladder were confirmed on this page alone; whether other templates share them is unverified.
Vertical rhythm was measured within the article band and across band boundaries; spacing inside the nav overlay, the cookie banner and the mobile menu was not captured.
